rationale: One MAJOR finding: blur() is called unconditionally, including on keyboard activation (Enter/Space). After a keyboard user presses Enter to copy, focus is discarded to document.body and the button disappears, breaking WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order. Fix: guard with `if (e.detail > 0)` so blur fires only on pointer clicks. All AC criteria pass except AC-6 (unit-only verification — CSS overlay interaction not covered). No security, contract, or correctness issues.

findings.problem: blur() is called unconditionally on every click event, including keyboard activation (Enter/Space). After a keyboard user presses Enter to trigger copy, focus is silently moved to document.body and the button disappears, leaving the user without a visual anchor. This violates WCAG 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
findings.impact: Keyboard-only users lose their navigation position after activating the Copy button. Screen reader users receive no post-action focus indication.
findings.recommendation: Guard the blur() call with a pointer-click check using e.detail: `if (e.detail > 0) { (e.currentTarget as HTMLElement).blur() }`. Mouse clicks have e.detail > 0; keyboard activations (Enter/Space) have e.detail === 0 in all major browsers.
